article.title: A Bigger Number Is Not Always Better
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Business reports often use arrows to show whether a number went up or down. An upward arrow can look positive, but a bigger number is not always better. The meaning depends on the metric. More sales, more retained customers, or more successful deliveries may be good. More complaints, more defects, more waiting time, or more fraud cases are usually bad. Some metrics are even more complicated. Higher average order value can be positive if customers are buying more useful products, but it can also rise because low-spending customers stopped buying. More screen time can mean strong engagement, or it can mean that users are struggling to finish a task. Before judging a KPI, analysts should ask what behavior the number represents and how it connects to the real business goal. They should also check whether another important metric became worse. For example, a campaign may increase clicks while also increasing unsubscribe rates. A call center may reduce average handling time while customers need to call again more often. This is why teams use guardrail metrics together with a main KPI. The main KPI describes the desired direction, while guardrails help detect harmful side effects. Targets also need context. A larger inventory may protect against shortages, but too much inventory ties up cash. A lower approval time is useful only if quality remains acceptable. Good analysis therefore does not celebrate movement automatically. It explains why a metric should move, what trade-offs may appear, and whether the underlying outcome improved. Numbers do not have a good or bad direction by themselves. Their meaning comes from the decision and system they represent. Analysts should define the population, observation window, and decision rule before interpreting the result. A useful review separates the observed pattern from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow.
paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文重點在於把 model metric 或 KPI 放回實際 decision context。數字變大不一定更好；極端群體可能自然回歸平均；ranking 與 probability calibration 是不同能力；歷史資料也會承載舊政策；而 campaign 真正關心的常常是 intervention 所創造的增量效果。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：model metricやKPIはdecision contextの中で解釈する必要がある。数値が大きいこと自体が良いとは限らず、極端群は平均へ回帰し、rankingとprobability calibrationは別の性能である。historical dataには旧policyも刻まれ、campaignではinterventionによる増分効果が重要になる。

business.term: Match the metric to the decision the business must make.
business.explanation: 讓指標與實際商業決策相匹配。

business.term: Estimate incremental value rather than observed response alone.
business.explanation: 不要只看觀察到的反應，應估計增量價值。
